basic_info.name: GD-Retriever / Generative Diffusion Retriever (GDR): Controllable Generative Text-Music Retrieval with Diffusion Models
basic_info.org: Julien Guinot, Elio Quinton, György Fazekas (Queen Mary University of London, Centre for Digital Music; likely with industry affiliation)
basic_info.release_date: arXiv 2506.17886, submitted 22 June 2025 (v2 24 June 2025); accepted at ISMIR 2025 (Seoul, poster P3-2, Sep 2025); paper under CC-BY-4.0 license.
basic_info.links: Paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2506.17886; Code: https://github.com/Pliploop/GDRetriever; ISMIR 2025 program page: https://ismir2025program.ismir.net/poster_48.html

architecture.backbone: Conditional latent diffusion model (UNet or MLP-based diffusion variants) that generates 'ghost' audio queries in a frozen retrieval-optimized latent space. Audio encoders: CLAP, MULE, or MusCALL audio towers; text encoders: T5 (Flan-T5) or CLAP text encoder. Trained on latent sequences of length T=64 (1 minute of audio), batch size 256, 100k steps, AdamW with linear warmup and cosine decay.
architecture.input_modality: text (English) conditions generation; retrieval corpus keys are audio embeddings (512-d frame sequences averaged over time and n_q=5 sampled queries).
architecture.training_objective: Diffusion (denoising) objective: train a diffusion model to map text embeddings to audio latent embeddings in a frozen audio-audio retrieval space, replacing contrastive cross-modal alignment with generative cross-modal bridging. No contrastive training of the retriever itself; minimizes reconstruction of target audio latents conditioned on text.
architecture.embedding_output: Queries are generated in the teacher's audio embedding space (512-d CLAP-style frame sequence latents, time-wise average pooling over T=64 frames and 5 samples into a single query embedding).

data.training_data: Trained on text-music caption datasets referenced via evaluation sets: SongDescriber, PrivateCaps, MusicCaps, and MTG-Jamendo-derived pairs; exact scale and full source enumeration not stated in reviewed sources [uncertain]. Audio latents come from frozen teacher encoders (CLAP / MULE / MusCALL audio towers), so no audio encoder training data of its own.

performance.benchmarks: Text-music retrieval (R@1/5/10 + CLAP-score): outperforms contrastive teacher models (CLAP, MusCALL, MULE) on in-domain datasets — most notably PrivateCaps (PC) and to a lesser extent SongDescriber (SD); performance degrades out-of-domain on MusicCaps (MC) for some variants (GDR-CLAP underperforms CLAP teacher on MC; GDR-MusCALL stronger than teacher on MC/SD). Example: GDR-CLAP w/ T5 text encoder achieves R@1 8.1, R@5 21.1, R@10 29.2 (vs CLAP-encoder variant 6.?/17.1/21.6) [uncertain on digit-level transcriptions]. Not evaluated on MuChoMusic/MusicBench.
performance.vs_clap: Mixed vs CLAP teacher: strong in-domain gains (esp. PrivateCaps), weaker/behind teacher out-of-domain (MusicCaps). Also: GDR-MULE (non-jointly-trained MULE audio space + T5 text) outperforms the CLAP teacher on PrivateCaps and SongDescriber, showing joint spaces can be built from audio-only latents.

availability.license: Paper CC-BY-4.0. Code public (MIT-style license likely, official implementation repo) [uncertain on license of repo code/diffusion checkpoints]. No large checkpoints of its own beyond the diffusion retriever over frozen teacher encoders.

fit_for_local_playlist.sample_rate: N/A at retriever level — operates on frozen teacher embeddings (CLAP/MULE/MusCALL audio towers); inherits teacher sample rates (CLAP/HTSAT 16k or 48k, MULE 16k) [uncertain].
fit_for_local_playlist.inference_cost: Small diffusion head (MLP or small UNet) over frozen encoders; ~5 diffusion query generations per text query, so per-query cost = text encode + 5 short diffusion denoise passes; only new text-side cost is added at query time — audio embeddings computed once. No published latency; CPU-feasible for MLP variant [uncertain].
fit_for_local_playlist.full_track_context: Trained with T=64 latent frames covering 1 minute of audio with averaged pooling; full-track (multi-minute) queries would need windowed extension [uncertain].
fit_for_local_playlist.frame_level_support: Internally frame-sequence (per-second) latents are averaged for retrieval; no exposed frame-level retrieval interface [uncertain].
fit_for_local_playlist.multilingual_queries: English (T5/CLAP English text towers); no multilingual support claimed.
fit_for_local_playlist.retrieval_steering: Yes, primary contribution: generative control — negative prompting (suppress attributes via negative prompt), DDIM inversion for interactive query refinement (modify an attribute while preserving the rest of the query semantics), and post-hoc manipulation of retrieval behavior; works even over audio-only latent spaces with arbitrary text encoders. This directly matches interactive playlist refinement use case.
